summary: The report examines power grid vulnerabilities from extreme weather, cyber-attacks, aging equipment and rising demand, using the September 23, 2023 Metro City blackout as a case study. It argues that smart grid technology, including smart meters and distributed energy resources, supported by policy like the Energy Modernization Act, can make grids more resilient. Success stories from New Parksville and Island State, plus the Highland City project, illustrate the benefits, and the report closes by urging a proactive, collaborative culture.
one_line: A report on power grid vulnerabilities, the September 2023 Metro City blackout, and how smart grid technology, policy and collaboration can build resilience.
key_facts: On September 23, 2023, a power outage hit the Metro City area, leaving over two million residents without power for approximately 12 hours.
Utility spokesperson Amanda Lin said the Metro City outage was triggered by heavy storms combined with a failure in a critical transformer substation.
Investigation found the Metro City substation had lacked essential upgrades that could have prevented the failure.
The outage disrupted public transportation, caused significant data losses for businesses, and jeopardized hospital functions.

A National Infrastructure Institute study published October 14, 2023 said the average age of transformers in the United States is around 40 years, with some as old as 70 years, well beyond design life.
Smart meters record power usage in real time and immediately notify the utility of interruptions, so outages can be pinpointed and handled faster.
Distributed energy resource systems (DERs) let homes and businesses generate their own electricity via solar panels, wind turbines and other means, reducing demand and providing backup power.
On November 12, 2023, New Parksville announced a 30% reduction in outage times compared to the previous year thanks to smart grid technology.

Island State reported only minimal outages in the last hurricane season, which Patricia Kim, director of the Island State Energy Office, attributed to its upgraded smart grid with real-time monitoring and automation.

The Energy Modernization Act, passed December 5, 2023 by the federal government, earmarked substantial investments for smart grid research and implementation, focusing on vulnerable and underserved regions.
EcoFlow Solutions announced on January 22, 2024 a Highland City project to protect the grid and incorporate demand response programs and real-time energy monitoring across its districts.
The report says smart grid benefits extend beyond reliability to energy efficiency, consumer empowerment and national security.
